title: Power Pages: plugin for GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code edits traditional sites
summary: The indirect-cost-only rating conflicts with documented pay-per-token billing for the Claude Code configuration the briefing discusses. The roadmap details and download/upload controls are supported; the governance checklist also names checks that have no controls-table rows.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is in development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists November CY2026 for general availability.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists October CY2026 for preview.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Developer.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Developer"]

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap product is Power Pages.
claims.quote: "products": ["Power Pages"]

claims.claim: The planned plugin capability creates and edits traditional non-SPA Power Pages sites using GitHub Copilot CLI or Claude Code.
claims.quote: The Power Pages plugin for GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code now supports creating and editing traditional (non-SPA) Power Pages sites.

claims.claim: Developers can use natural-language prompts to create a traditional site.
claims.quote: Developers can use natural-language prompts in their AI coding agent to create a new traditional site

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The agent workflow can download, inspect and update existing site metadata.
claims.quote: download, inspect, and update existing site metadata

claims.claim: Editable metadata includes web pages, web templates, content snippets, basic and multistep forms, lists, table permissions, web roles and site settings.
claims.quote: such as web pages, web templates, content snippets, basic and multistep forms, lists, table permissions, web roles, and site settings

claims.claim: Changes are uploaded back to the environment using the Power Platform CLI.
claims.quote: then upload changes back to their environment using the Power Platform CLI.

claims.claim: The current Learn plugin guidance describes modern SPA sites.
claims.quote: provides an AI-assisted workflow for creating, deploying, and managing modern single-page application (SPA) sites on Power Pages.

claims.claim: Learn warns that AI-generated code and configuration can be inaccurate.
claims.quote: Code and configuration generated by the AI coding agent can be inaccurate.

claims.claim: Learn says to review, test and validate generated content before approving or deploying it.
claims.quote: Review, test, and validate all generated content before you approve or deploy it. Always review agent proposals before approving them.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Table permissions assigned to web roles control access to Dataverse data.
claims.quote: Table permissions assigned to web roles allow members of the web role to access data that's stored in Dataverse tables.

claims.claim: Granting the Anonymous users web role table access can expose the table's data to any site visitor.
claims.quote: When the Anonymous users web role is granted access to a table, any user who visits the site can access the data in the table.

claims.claim: The workflow introduces a third-party AI coding tool through Claude Code.
claims.quote: Anthropic's Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools.

claims.claim: Downloaded site metadata and configuration are stored on the developer's local file system.
claims.quote: Support for download/upload of website configuration data to/from the local file system

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: GitHub usage including GitHub Copilot can be billed through the Azure subscription linked to a GitHub organization.
claims.quote: All GitHub usage from that organization — including GitHub Copilot and GitHub Actions — flows to that subscription.

claims.claim: The documented Microsoft Foundry configuration for Claude Code requires a paid Azure subscription.
claims.quote: To use Claude models in Microsoft Foundry, you must have a paid Azure subscription with a billing account in a country or region where Anthropic offers the models for purchase.

claims.claim: Claude Code billing depends on the service it is configured with, including a billable Microsoft Foundry configuration.
claims.quote: Claude models use Global Standard deployments with pay-per-token billing, so idle deployments don't incur charges.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No plugin-specific Microsoft price is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin GitHub Copilot CLI Claude Code licensing pricing license requirements; pricing meter free. Read plugin prerequisites, Power Pages licensing and licensing FAQ; no plugin-specific price found.

claims.claim: The plugin-specific licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin GitHub Copilot CLI Claude Code licensing pricing license requirements. Read plugin prerequisites, Power Pages licensing and licensing FAQ; published site-access licensing does not state an entitlement for this external plugin.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: developers choose to install and use the plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin GitHub Copilot CLI Claude Code tenant admin disable enable policy Power Platform API pac admin. Read plugin Install the plugin and Copilot hub; installation is developer-initiated and no plugin-specific enabling switch was found.

claims.claim: VS Code Power Platform Tools provides Explorer > Power Pages Actions > Active Sites > site (right-click) > Download / Upload.
claims.quote: Power Pages Actions is available in the pane titled Power Pages Actions in the Explorer sidebar of Visual Studio Code. ... Upload: Uploads local changes back to your environment. ... Download: Downloads the site content to a local folder for offline editing.

claims.claim: pac pages download accepts --path, --webSiteId and --modelVersion, and pac pages upload accepts --path and --modelVersion for site content transfer.
claims.quote: pac pages download --path "C:\portals" --webSiteId f88b70cc-580b-4f1a-87c3-41debefeb902 --modelVersion 2 ... pac pages upload --path "C:\portals\starter-portal" --modelVersion 2

claims.claim: The plugin uses an authenticated Power Platform CLI session connected to the developer's target environment.
claims.quote: An authenticated PAC CLI session connected to your target environment.

claims.claim: Dataverse data operations are constrained by the authenticated user's security roles and privileges.
claims.quote: Your code will only be able to perform operations based on the privileges assigned to the user account through security roles or team membership.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a tenant admin switch specifically for the coding-agent plugin on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin tenant disable PowerShell API coding agent; plugin tenant admin disable enable policy Power Platform API pac admin. Read plugin guidance and Copilot hub; its Prodev control names the VS Code extension, not this external plugin.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Power Platform CLI supports tracking site configuration changes and checking configuration into source control.
claims.quote: You can now check in the website configuration to source control and move the website configuration to any environment using Microsoft Power Platform CLI.

claims.claim: Code sites also use the authenticated Power Platform CLI workflow for uploading and downloading assets.
claims.quote: Power Pages SPA sites are managed using the PAC CLI commands upload-code-site and download-code-site.

claims.claim: A plugin-specific upload identifier in the admin center is not documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin upload audit identifier admin center Claude Code GitHub Copilot. Read plugin deployment and ALM guidance, CLI reference, and Copilot hub; no admin-center upload identifier specific to the plugin found.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist tells readers to check has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Run table permission audits after agent changes. Review who has installed the plugin and which environments they target. The table contains only downloading/uploading content and the missing tenant admin switch.
claims.fix: Remove the two After rollout bullets: table permission audits and reviewing plugin installations and target environments have no corresponding controls-table rows. Do not add rows as part of this correction.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The low cost rating represents indirect review time only despite the briefing's documented Claude Code billing option.
claims.quote: Page: cost: "low"; "Developer time for review is the main known cost." Learn: "Claude models use Global Standard deployments with pay-per-token billing, so idle deployments don't incur charges."
claims.fix: Set cost to variable. Replace the final Cost and licensing sentence with 'Review time is an additional indirect cost; Claude Code configured with Microsoft Foundry uses pay-per-token billing.' Replace the cost rationale with 'Variable. Coding-agent charges depend on the provider and plan; Claude Code configured with Microsoft Foundry uses pay-per-token billing. No plugin-specific price is published.' Keep the existing Foundry source.
